source.name: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open however often Escape is pressed
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/43070) at 2bb544eb426e9b1e019c2a98798e0002b8a41d35, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

journey.title: Escape must not dismiss a dialog opened with keyboard: false
journey.goal: The confirmation dialog stays open however often Escape is pressed, so the user can still enter the code and send the transfer

functionalJourney.title: Confirm with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking the backdrop does not close the dialog; entering the code and clicking Send completes the transfer

guards.title: Cancel transfer still closes the dialog from the keyboard
guards.goal: Tabbing to Cancel transfer and pressing Enter closes the dialog and records the cancellation

plan.root_cause: The Escape key's cancel event becomes non-cancelable after repeated activations, causing the dialog to close unexpectedly when keyboard:false. This occurs because the native cancel event (which fires only for modal dialogs) loses its cancelable property, so preventDefault() has no effect and the dialog's default close action proceeds.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener in DialogBase._addDialogListeners to prevent default and return early when keyboard:false, regardless of modal status, thereby consuming the Escape key before it triggers a cancel event.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer dismiss the dialog when opened with keyboard:false, allowing users to remain focused on the OTP input and complete the transfer without accidental closure.
functional_risks: Consumers who rely on the cancel event firing for Escape when keyboard:false will no longer receive that event.
verification_requirements: Pressing Escape any number of times must not close the dialog when keyboard:false.
Pressing Escape must still close the dialog when keyboard:true.
The dialog must still be dismissible via the Cancel button and via submitting a correct six‑digit OTP.
